title: PhD Position in Macroeconomics, DFG Project "Stabilization, Risk Sharing, and Debt Sustainability" (w/m/d)
industry: Public Economics & Economic Policy (JEL H), Economics, Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics (JEL E), Economics and Social Sciences, Econometrics, Statistics and Quantitative Methods (JEL C)
text:
Your tasks
We are seeking a highly motivated doctoral researcher to join our dynamic research group and contribute to this DFG-funded project. The successful candidate is expected to conduct original research within the project's work packages leading to a doctoral dissertation, and to present their findings at departmental seminars and international conferences. The position further involves communication activities, including policy briefs, a project website and contributions to public debates.
Your profile
An excellent Master's level degree in Economics or related fields with a strong background in macroeconomics and/or numerical methods (students close to completing their Master's degree are also encouraged to apply)
Strong quantitative and programming skills (MATLAB, Python, Dynare, or similar)
Interest in fiscal federalism, monetary unions, and/or quantitative macroeconomic modelling
Ability to work both independently and as part of a research team
Excellent collaboration skills with flexibility and strong teamwork
Very good written and spoken communication skills in both German and English
What sets us apart
Vibrant and innovative working environment on a green campus with everything at close quarters
Multi-faceted and responsible role with creative freedom
Secure position
Very good work/life balance
Flexible working hours & remote working
Wide range of opportunities for personal and professional development
Health support & university sport
Job ticket & Job bike
Working environment
As a university with a distinct profile, the University of Hohenheim brings together the Faculties of Agricultural Sciences, Natural Sciences, and Business, Economics and Social Sciences. Our green campus with everything at close quarters promotes collaboration and creates an inspiring environment for research, teaching, and work. With us, aspiring minds find a community in which they can grow and develop. Shape a sustainable future with us!
Equal opportunities and diversity are important to us. Your skills and strengths count for us – regardless of age, gender, origin, or religion. We welcome applications from people with severe disabilities or equivalent; if suitable, we will give them preferential consideration.
Have we sparked your interest?
We look forward to receiving your application via our online portal. If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us: Prof. Dr. Michael P. Evers, Einrichtungsleitung 520A, Phone Number 0711 459 22591.
